diagnosis: The primary issue lies in how the tokenizer processes tokens following special symbols or comments. Specifically, when encountering a semicolon (`;`), which denotes the start of a comment, the code incorrectly parses subsequent characters as separate tokens instead of treating them as part of the same token or ignoring them entirely. This misclassification leads to erroneous outputs where non-token entities are identified as valid tokens.

causal_chain: The test case `source_s4_mr2` with input `;` followed by `6#l` and a newline expects only the numeric token `93`, but instead processes `6#l` as an invalid token.
This indicates that after processing the semicolon (comment start), the tokenizer fails to correctly reset or handle subsequent characters, leading to incorrect parsing.
mr_refs: The function `is_token_end()` at line 218 incorrectly identifies the end of tokens when in comment mode (`str_com_id>2`), causing improper tokenization after a semicolon.
testcase_refs: Test case `source_s4_mr2` fails because it processes `6#l` as an invalid token instead of ignoring it.

assumption: The tokenizer incorrectly continues parsing after a semicolon, mistaking subsequent characters as valid tokens.

expected_effect: Prevents incorrect tokenization after semicolon by properly ending comment processing and resetting state, ensuring subsequent characters are not parsed as tokens until the next valid start condition.

repair_intent: Ensure that after a semicolon (comment start), only the comment is processed and subsequent characters are treated appropriately without forming invalid tokens.
